newsitem.title: UK: Third World gold demand is up again-WGC.
newsitem.headline: Third World gold demand is up again-WGC.

text.p: Total gold demand from countries in Asia, the Middle East and Latin America monitored by the World Gold Council (WGC) soared again to set a new record for the third quarter, the WGC said.
The main feature was that Latin American demand rose 13 percent as the economies of the region continued a recovery.
In the Asian developing markets demand was unchanged overall in 1996 from the high 1995 third quarter level but there were notable changes among individual countries.

Vietnam showed the strongest growth during the quarter with a 67-percent increase, Indonesia was up 39 percent, Malaysia up 15 percent and South Korea up eight percent but Chinese offtake slipped six percent and Taiwan was down 27 percent.

Turkish demand reached a three-year high after rising 15 percent, but demand from the Middle East Gulf was down 10 percent due to weakness in Saudi Arabia. Indian demand was four percent lower reflecting delayed festival season buying.

In the developed countries, European demand was up one percent to its highest third quarter level in four years and U.S. demand was up four percent to a new third quarter record buoyed by jewellery offtake
But in Japan the retreat of investment demand brought a 29-percent collapse in consumption.
The WGC is backed by a number of gold producers and monitors gold demand in countries accounting for about 75 percent of world gold consumption. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7729
